howBytesWereMeasured.pixels: pdftoppm -r 300 -gray -f N -l N -singlefile, writing binary P5 PGM directly; never -png. The reader asserts the magic is P5 and that maxval is 255, parses the header arithmetically and reads the raster with numpy. Ink threshold: grey < 200, with every reading repeated at grey < 128 so a finding cannot be an anti-aliasing artefact. Scope: whole delivered page at 2550 x 3300 px, and named rectangles inside it converted from PDF top-left points at 300/72 px per point.
howBytesWereMeasured.howOverlayINKWasSEPARATEDfromPRINTEDink: The Florida source binary is not in this container, so the pinned blank cannot be rendered. Instead each delivered fixture was opened with pdf-lib and the LAST content stream of each page removed. pdf-lib appends its drawing as a separate final stream: pages 1-3 carry /Contents arrays of four streams (2, 37218, 2, 2012 / 2, 27423, 2, 325 / 2, 24111, 2, 545 bytes) and pages 4-5 carry a single stream and no overlay at all. Dropping the last element yields a source-equivalent page. addedInk = ink in the delivered render AND NOT in the stripped render.
howBytesWereMeasured.positiveControlBeforeEveryZero: Every zero below was read in the same run as a positive control. Whole-page control, canonical, grey<200: pages 1, 2, 3 read 32,268 / 6,359 / 4,401 added ink px and pages 4 and 5 read 0 -- and 0 is the correct answer on 4 and 5, because those pages carry no overlay stream at all. Rectangle control on page 3: the surname's own word box read 908 added px in the same run in which a blank margin box of the same height read 0.
howBytesWereMeasured.aLIMITofTHISDETECTORstatedRATHERthanHIDD: addedInk is blind inside pixels the source already inks. Overlay ink painted exactly on top of a printed rule reads as 0 added, not because nothing was painted but because the pixel was already dark. That is why the agency finding is reported as 17 px ABOVE the rule with 0 px INSIDE the rule band: the 0 is a masked reading, not an absence.
howBytesWereMeasured.glyphs: For Nebraska, scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-output-glyph-reading.mjs, which decompresses each flattened widget Form XObject out of the produced bytes and counts the glyphs its show-text operators draw. Not the builder's write intent.

theType0Measurement.whyThisIsHere: VF42 established that scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-pdf-anchor-capture.mjs line 260 reads `subtype === "Type0"` where subtype stringifies a PDFName and therefore carries a leading slash, so the test is permanently false and CID widths are never read. VF42 then measured, on NE DC-1-15 alone, that repairing it changes 113 widths and 0 decoded strings, and concluded the repair 'may be width-only, which makes it a smaller job than FIX140 concluded'. This lane tested that conclusion, because it decides whether Nebraska can be rebuilt.
theType0Measurement.whatThisLaneRan: Both module versions -- the committed one and one differing ONLY in `subtype` -> `subtypeName` on line 260 -- were imported side by side and extractTextItems was run over every page of 308 corpus PDFs, 994,533 text runs, comparing text and width run for run.
theType0Measurement.theWidthResult: null-width runs 119,883 -> 980, a 99.2% reduction; 118,903 widths change; 244 of 308 files change at least one width. On NE DC-1-15 specifically: 249 runs, 214 null before and 0 after, 214 widths changed, 0 texts changed. VF42's 113 on page 1 plus 101 on page 2 is exactly this lane's 214, reproduced independently.
theType0Measurement.theTEXTresultTHATREFUTEStheNARROWCONCLUS: 14,179 runs change TEXT, across 130 of the 308 files. The changes are corruption, not correction: NE CC-6-11A reads 'b', 'nt', 'er ', 'he ', 'rig' under the committed module and '\u4500', '\u6e34', '\u6572 ', '\u6865 ', '\u7269\u6700' under the fixed one, and AK TF-805, NV RCCD, VT 200-00130A, four RI motions, four NC AOC forms and 120 others do the same.
theType0Measurement.whyItCorrupts: Both DC-1-15 and CC-6-11A use Identity-H, so the CMap is not the difference. The difference is that CC-6-11A's content stream splits two-byte codes ACROSS string operands, so a run can arrive with an odd number of bytes. glyphsOf with step 2 then pairs the wrong bytes. The committed module survives that by walking one byte per glyph and letting collapseUtf16BE merge pairs afterwards, which only works when the NUL falls on even indices.
theType0Measurement.theCORRECTIONtoVF42: VF42's measurement is right and its generalisation is not, and the counter-example is INSIDE THE SAME NEBRASKA FAMILY. DC-1-15 is width-only; CC-6-11a, one of this family's own four bound documents, is not. The honest statement is the one the module's own comment makes and FIX140 made: the repair is a decoding change, not a measurement change. It needs the walker to carry a partial multi-byte code across string operands, which is real surgery on a module with 214 importers in scripts/ alone.
theType0Measurement.whatItWOULDbuy: Measured, not guessed. With the slash change alone and nothing else, the Nebraska build's refusal goes from FOUR unnamed blanks to ONE: Text44 recovers the caption '__________________________, Judge of the ___________________', Text46 recovers '__________________ County Courthouse or Justice Center,', Text1 recovers 'I' under the region heading 'Certificate of Service', and only Text74 (',verify that on', the certificate-of-service date) remains unnamed. With that one field named the family builds to completion, with the page order corrected in the delivered bytes and every glyph reading real. That is what a lane that owns the module would unblock.
theType0Measurement.whyThisLaneDIDNOTLANDit: A two-family repair grant is not authority to change the decoding of 214 importers, and this lane's own measurement says a naive change corrupts 130 of 308 corpus forms. The module was restored to its committed bytes; `git status` is clean of it and nothing in either commit touches it. This is dispatch material for Captain, not a fix to slip in.
theType0Measurement.reproduceIt: The experiment is a one-character edit to line 260 and a side-by-side import; no state was left behind.

SOURCE_IDENTITY.howThatWasEstablished: Every pin in this family directory was walked BY SHAPE -- any object carrying a repository-path key beside a sha256, in any container, not only groundingRecords. Ten were found, across source-receipt.json (mountedReadOnlySource and all four authorityRecords), reports/rendered-artifacts.json (pdfs[0..1] and artifacts[0..1]) and product-wiring.json (proposedRepresentation.components[0]). Every in-repository pin RECOMPUTES TO ITS PINNED DIGEST at HEAD: CODEX_CS2_SRC2_ACQUISITION.json 061f4c5f, FL.memo.json 9b497440, FL-florida.json ffef299b, route-obligation-candidate.json f6fc0814, and both fixtures. This family also does not appear in data/rcap-grade-a/source-identity/COMMITTED_RECORD_PIN_DRIFT_2026-09-04.json, so it was not among the 34 pins Captain swept.
SOURCE_IDENTITY.theRealFinding: Read from the review's own text rather than a summary: the family binds FDLE 40-028 printed 'Revised October 2019', while the official Florida Administrative Code reference Ref-14426, used by rule 11C-7.010 effective 08/30/2023, exposes a five-page FDLE 40-028 printed 'Revised June 2021' whose parsed text adds approved fingerprint vendors on pages 3 and 5 and expressly requires physical paper rather than electronic submission on page 5. Those are substantive procedural additions absent from the 2019 edition this family renders.
SOURCE_IDENTITY.notRepaired: A build lane does not decide which edition the issuer's rule adopts, and the reviewer expressly left 'obtaining and hashing the adopted raw binary' outstanding. This container cannot obtain it: network egress to the Florida sources is blocked (flsenate.gov returned EGRESS_BLOCKED from the proxy when this lane tried to read the statute), and the 2021 blank is not in the mounted corpus, whose FL folder holds FDLE 40-021 and 40-026 only.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.measured: Both committed guides presented the $75 as unconditional. Neither contained the words 'waive', 'waiver' or 'executive director'.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.whatTheGUIDESSAYNOW: The fee is paid unless the executive director of FDLE waives it; section 943.0515, Florida Statutes, provides for that waiver and gives the decision to the executive director; ask FDLE's Seal & Expunge Section for the current waiver-request instructions; until a waiver is actually granted the $75 is still owed and goes in with the packet; and this is not a court fee-waiver motion, not an indigency finding, and not the juvenile-diversion fee exception.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.whatIsDELIBERATELYNOTSAID: The statute is NOT quoted. Egress to flsenate.gov is blocked in this container, so this lane did not read section 943.0515 and does not pretend to; what is carried is the finding of the independent review that did read it, and the guide attributes the rule to the section without putting words in it. The waiver REQUEST MECHANICS are stated nowhere, because no held source in this repository carries them, and the guide says so instead of inventing a procedure.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.theRECORDSOWNAMOUNT: $75, carried unchanged on both files and asserted by the guard.

SERVICE.measured: Both committed guides said 'the appropriate State Attorney or Statewide Prosecutor', singular, and neither contained the phrase 'every affected circuit'.
SERVICE.whatTheGUIDESSAYNOW: Where the included arrests or charges span more than one judicial circuit, section 943.0515 requires the approval of the prosecutor of EVERY affected circuit; this is a decision each office makes for itself and may refuse, not ordinary civil service; and the participant stops and gets help before sending anything if any required approval is missing or refused. Every prosecutor field, decision and signature remains blank.
SERVICE.notTested: The two committed fixtures are single-arrest, single-circuit. No multi-circuit branch was executed or claimed tested.
